question: Do the stage-03 price, the stage-03 exactness and the stage-08 anti-aliasing results hold on natural image content at a higher resolution than MNIST?
data: 15 OpenCV sample images (lena, baboon, fruits, board, building, butterfly, starry_night, HappyFish, messi5, chicky_512, sudoku, aero1, aero3, left01, home), converted to grey, two 64 x 64 crops per image (centre and a quarter-offset crop) that are not flat (std > 0.08): the first 20 such crops in file order.

zoos.recipe: PyTorch trainer (NumPy for the swing-bounded ones), 3,000 Adam steps at 1e-3, omega 30, first-layer init U(-1/2, 1/2) x 30

measurements: fit PSNR; Gaussian blur (1 px) and box footprint (4 px) programs on the function-space target (8x supersampled); anti-aliased x4 downsampling: point sampling, program, 2x2 and 4x4 supersampling against the footprint truth (stage-08 protocol at side 64)

predictions_frozen_before_running.N1_price_persists: At both parameter levels the deep family exceeds the shallow family by at least 4 dB median PSNR (the gap is expected to be smaller than on MNIST, whose digits are unusually compressible by composition).
predictions_frozen_before_running.N2_programs_exact: On both shallow zoos the Gaussian and box programs have function-space MSE below 1e-4 x no-edit MSE on every crop.
predictions_frozen_before_running.N3_antialias: On shallow_w1024 at x4, the program (1 spp) beats 4x4 supersampling (16 spp) by at least 15 dB.
predictions_frozen_before_running.N4_bounded_cost: deep_h64_swing4 is within 5 dB of deep_h64 in PSNR and its first-order blur ratio is at most 0.4; deep_h64_swing2 is within 10 dB and at most 0.2.
predictions_frozen_before_running.N5_standard_deep_not_programmable: deep_h64 first-order blur ratio is at least 0.7.
